name: Treaty with the Caddo, 1835
nations: Caddo Nation (Hasinai, Kadohadacho and allied peoples)
promises: Article I: the Caddo ceded all their land in north-western Louisiana and south-western Arkansas, between the Red River and the boundary with Mexico.
Article II: the Caddo agreed to move at their own expense out of the United States within one year and never return to live there as a nation.
Article III: $80,000 in all: $30,000 in goods and horses at signing, $10,000 within a year and $10,000 a year for the next four years.

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission found that the 617,967.4 acres ceded were worth an average of 75 cents an acre on January 26, 1836, when the treaty took effect, and that the $80,000 paid was an unconscionable consideration. It made an interlocutory award of $383,475.55, the difference, less any offsets.

breaches.what: After refusing in 1968 to let the government offset the value of the Caddo's later Oklahoma reservation (holding that the Caddo were settled there in discharge of a US duty to protect them, not as a gift), the Commission entered final judgment of $383,475.55 for the 1835 cession, with no offsets.

landTaken: 617,967.4 acres in north-western Louisiana and south-western Arkansas, as found by the Indian Claims Commission (Docket 226, 1960).
compensation: $80,000 under the treaty. The ICC found the land worth about $463,475 (75 cents an acre) and entered final judgment for $383,475.55 in 1977.
today: Removed beyond the then US border into Texas, the Caddo were later moved to a Texas reservation and in 1859 to the Wichita Reservation in present Oklahoma (ICC, 19 Ind. Cl. Comm. 385). The Caddo Nation is headquartered in Binger, Oklahoma.

openQuestions: The OCR of the 1960 order is damaged: it reads both 611,967.4 and 617,967.4 acres and a land value of '$b53,475.55'. The figures used here (617,967.4 acres, $0.75 an acre, about $463,475.55, award $383,475.55 after the $80,000 paid) are consistent with each other and with the 1977 final award, but the page image was not checked.
Caddo claims to lands in Texas and Oklahoma were dismissed for failure of proof in 1955 (4 Ind. Cl. Comm. 214).
